What is MLX?
MLX is Apple's array framework for running machine learning on Apple silicon. It uses unified memory so models can move between CPU and GPU without copying.

What does LoRA stand for?
LoRA stands for Low-Rank Adaptation. It freezes the base model and trains small low-rank matrices instead of all weights.

What is a quantized model?
A quantized model stores weights in fewer bits, such as 4-bit instead of 16-bit. It uses much less memory with a small loss in quality.

What is a learning rate?
The learning rate controls how much weights are updated per training step. Too high and training diverges; too low and it crawls.

Explain overfitting.
Overfitting is when a model memorizes training data and fails on new data. Regularization, more data, or stopping early helps.

What is an epoch in training?
An epoch is one full pass over the training dataset. Iteration or step is one optimizer update, which usually sees only a batch.

What is a token?
A token is a chunk of text a model reads, like a word or subword. Models split text into tokens with a tokenizer before training.

What is a transformer?
A transformer is a neural network built on attention, letting every token consider every other token. It powers most modern language models.

What does SLM mean?
SLM means small language model, typically under a few billion parameters. They run fast on-device and fine-tune cheaply.

What is gradient checkpointing?
Gradient checkpointing trades compute for memory by discarding activations and recomputing them during backprop. It reduces RAM use at the cost of speed.

What is a validation set?
A validation set is data held out from training to monitor generalization. It guides choices like when to stop and which checkpoint to keep.

What is perplexity?
Perplexity measures how surprised a model is by a text; lower is better. It roughly reflects the average branching factor per token.

What is a chat template?
A chat template formats messages with role markers like turn and end tokens. Training and inference must use the same template to match the model's expectations.

What is warmup in training?
Warmup raises the learning rate slowly over the first steps. It stabilizes early training and avoids large noisy updates at the start.

What is an adapter?
An adapter is a small set of extra weights trained on top of a frozen base model. At inference it can be merged into the base weights.

What does fine-tuning mean?
Fine-tuning continues training a pretrained model on a narrower dataset for a specific task. It adapts general knowledge to your data.

What is batch size?
Batch size is the number of examples processed before one weight update. Larger batches smooth gradients but need more memory.

What is unified memory?
Unified memory is one memory pool shared by the CPU and GPU on Apple silicon. Data can be used by both without copying between them.
